findings.location: alembic autogenerate drift against the live schema; CI runs upgrade head only (no check)
findings.line: env.py:20-22 (target_metadata = app.db.models.Base only; no include_object filters); models.py (42 index=True columns, 0 explicit Index() objects); CI: alembic upgrade head only
findings.finding: Executed `alembic check` at head 062 FAILS against the live database: 7 removed tables (checkpoint_blobs, checkpoint_migrations, checkpoints, checkpoint_writes — created at runtime by LangGraph saver.setup(); chat_messages, lessons, audit_log — live app tables absent from env.py metadata), 55 removed indexes (including HNSW vector indexes code_embeddings_embedding_hnsw and versioned_lessons_embedding_hnsw), 1 added index, 2 removed + 2 added unique constraints. Any developer merging `alembic revision --autogenerate` today produces a migration proposing to DROP live tables/indexes.
findings.evidence: Command executed 2026-10-02: `.venv/bin/alembic check` -> failure; unique removed-table list {audit_log, chat_messages, checkpoint_blobs, checkpoint_migrations, checkpoints, checkpoint_writes, lessons} = 7; `grep -c 'Detected removed index'` = 55; added index = 1; removed unique = 2; added unique = 2. `alembic current` = 062 = head (applied state itself is correct).
findings.production_impact: A routine autogenerated migration merged into main would propose destructive drops: checkpoint* breaks run resume and history; chat_messages/lessons/audit_log destroys chat memory, lessons and the audit trail. Silent, high-blast-radius data loss on a future deploy.
findings.recommendation: Add metadata include_object/include_name filters for runtime/vector/legacy objects, declare ORM models + Index() for app-owned tables (chat_messages, lessons, audit_log, HNSW indexes), and add `alembic check` as a CI gate so drift fails builds.

findings.location: RTO/RPO targets undefined; only dev-scale timings measured
findings.line: disaster_recovery.md (207 lines; no RTO/RPO section); timer OnCalendar=03:00 + RandomizedDelaySec=1800
findings.finding: No recovery time objective or recovery point objective is stated anywhere. Measured this audit at dev scale: backup ~1.8 s (4.84 MB dump, 444 TOC entries), restore ~7.5 s into a disposable DB with identical counts. The shipped daily cadence (03:00 + up to 30 min splay) implies a worst-case RPO of ~24 h + <=30 min by design. Production-scale restore time, partial/point-in-time recovery and offsite loss scenarios are unmeasured.
findings.evidence: Drill 2026-10-02 (see drill_evidence); grep for RTO/RPO in docs/ and scripts/ -> no defined targets.
findings.production_impact: Undefined recovery expectations for a real incident; a 24 h data-loss window may be unacceptable for a paid product but that decision has never been made.
findings.recommendation: Human decision: set RTO/RPO targets; if finer RPO is required, move to WAL archiving / more frequent dumps (brief §237 gate: 'RTO/RPO MEASURED OR HUMAN-DEFINED').

findings.location: backup automation shipped but dormant; zero backup artifacts exist
findings.line: gridiron-backup.timer (03:00, splay 1800 s, Persistent=true, not installed); docker-compose.prod.yml has no backup service
findings.finding: The backup script is drill-proven, but nothing in this environment (or in the deployed artifacts) actually runs it: `systemctl list-timers gridiron-backup.timer` -> 0 timers; no gridiron unit in /etc/systemd/system; /var/backups/gridiron absent; ./backups absent. The unit header documents manual install (cp + systemctl edit for DATABASE_URL/BACKUP_DIR + enable --now). No component alerts if a backup is missed.
findings.evidence: Executed 2026-10-02: systemctl list-timers -> '0 timers listed'; ls /etc/systemd/system | grep -i gridiron -> empty; ls /var/backups/gridiron -> No such file or directory; ls repo/backups -> No such file or directory.
findings.production_impact: For any host where the operator has not performed the manual install, the system has NO backups at all — total data-loss exposure upon disk loss, while documentation implies backups exist.
findings.recommendation: Install the timer per its header on the DB host (or add a compose backup service), document it in DEPLOYMENT.md as a required production step, and add 'backup age' alerting.

findings.line: prod migrate one-shot service runs `alembic upgrade head` (on-failure); DEPLOYMENT.md describes the deploy order but prescribes no pre-migration snapshot
findings.finding: The migration step runs immediately with no preceding dump. Combined with PROD-13-103 (possibly no recent backup), a destructive or failed migration has no guaranteed rollback point; recovery relies on the restore procedure being fed a dump that may not exist.
findings.evidence: docker-compose.prod.yml migrate service (one-shot, on-failure); no backup step in DEPLOYMENT.md's procedure; backup timer dormant (PROD-13-103).
findings.production_impact: A bad migration can force losing everything since the last available backup (possibly none) instead of a minutes-old snapshot.
findings.recommendation: Wrap migrate in 'take dump -> verify pg_restore --list -> upgrade', or document a mandatory operator pre-step in DEPLOYMENT.md.

findings.finding: There is no in-product quiesce path. During restores, destructive repairs or migrations, the API keeps accepting new tasks/agent runs; in-flight work is neither drained nor rejected with an explanatory 503. Operators must stop services externally, and DEPLOYMENT.md does not describe a maintenance sequence.
findings.evidence: grep -ri maintenance over backend/app -> 0 hits; DEPLOYMENT.md (174 lines) has no maintenance-mode section.
findings.production_impact: Recovery operations can race with new writes/LLM spend; restore-under-load risks inconsistent post-restore state.
findings.recommendation: Add a maintenance flag that rejects new task starts with 503 + Retry-After while letting in-flight work drain; document the runbook.

findings.location: secret rotation is runbook-only and never exercised; no rotation tooling
findings.line: disaster_recovery.md secret rotation table; no rotation script in scripts/
findings.finding: A rotation runbook (which secret, where used, blast radius) exists, but there is no tooling to execute rotation, no rotation was ever performed, and the Fernet vault key re-wrap path is untested. Secret-leak history scan (577 commits, git log -S) surfaced only fixture values in samples ('sk-ant-test-key', 'FAKEFA', 'AKIAABCDEFGHIJ', 'ghp_faketoke', 'ghp_xxxxxxxx') — sampled, not exhaustive.
findings.evidence: disaster_recovery.md rotation table; ls scripts/ -> no rotation script; git log -S samples resolved to fixtures only.
findings.production_impact: A real leak would require an improvised manual rotation across .env, compose, vault key and provider consoles with no rehearsal.
findings.recommendation: Write a rotation script or a step-by-step checklist with expected outputs; rehearse once in a non-prod environment.

verified_clean_summary: RESTORE_VERIFIED executed: pg_dump -Fc (4.84 MB / 444 TOC / ~1.8 s) restored into a disposable DB with pg_restore --exit-on-error (OK ~7.5 s) and identical row counts (alembic 1@062, dev_tasks 414, agent_runs 91, task_logs 108); cleanup verified (throwaway DB dropped, dump removed, live DB unchanged).

Orphan recovery is real and wired: stale heartbeat sweep (300 s) resumes resolvable runs from checkpoints or fails+escalates the rest and, per the audit-13 addition, blocks the task (blocked_reason='orphaned') so it cannot sit 'running' in the UI forever; leader-gated loop + startup OS-process sweep + startup mark-failed behavior verified at cited lines.

DB-outage error contract: is_db_unavailable classifier -> 503 + Retry-After: 5 with the app's JSON shape (main.py:1907-1925), applied consistently (rbac.py:44-45, auth.py:95); HTTP exception handler preserves headers (main.py:1941-1948).

Cost runaway control: hard daily LLM cap checked before dispatch (spend_guard.check_before_dispatch:168) with Redis INCRBYFLOAT ledger + in-process fallback and DailyBudgetExceeded surfaced to callers; disable-by-design when COST_BUDGET_DAILY_USD<=0; installed at the shared client wrapper so all call sites inherit it.
Provider fault tolerance: shared Anthropic circuit breaker applied to the SDK call wrapper (base_graph.py:44,166-167) plus dedicated outage/retry tests committed.
Abuse control: slowapi rate limiting incl. a dedicated login/refresh brute-force limit (auth.py:67,167; config.py:2141).

Graceful shutdown: lifespan cancels and awaits ~20+ background tasks (incl. orphan_recovery_task.cancel() main.py:1806; gather :1828-1834), disposes the leader-election engine and closes the 3 LangGraph checkpointer connections.

Data lifecycle: leader-gated retention loop (main.py:1439); admin-only destructive surface — DELETE /privacy/user/{username} behind require_admin (privacy.py:132-135), exports self or admin (:103,:120-123).

Prod deployment hygiene: logs bounded at 20 m per service (docker-compose.prod.yml:48); Redis AOF + redisdata volume in prod (:76,:78,:229); QUEUE_BACKEND=rq default (:115); ANTHROPIC_API_KEY required (:116,:176); migrate one-shot on-failure; pool_pre_ping=True (db/session.py:49,87).

Backup/restore script mechanics: pg_restore --list integrity check, .partial rename-on-success, retention pruning (default 30), --exit-on-error restore with post-check of alembic_version — all verified by script reading plus the executed drill.

Secret history scan (577 commits, sampled): all git log -S hits examined resolve to test fixtures (sk-ant-test-key, FAKEFA, AKIAABCDEFGHIJ, ghp_faketoke, ghp_xxxxxxxx); no live-looking credential found in samples.
